content: Does the University of Sheffield offer on-campus counseling or therapy services, and how are these services funded and staffed?

Yes, the University of Sheffield offers on-campus counseling or therapy services. These services are provided by the University's Counselling Service, which is staffed by fully qualified and experienced counsellors.

The Counselling Service is funded by the University and is available free of charge to all current students. The Service is funded through the University's Student Services Budget, which is allocated each year to support a range of student support services, including counseling and mental health services.

The Counselling Service also operates in partnership with external mental health services, such as the NHS, to ensure that students have access to a range of appropriate support and treatment options.

Overall, the University of Sheffield is committed to supporting the mental health and wellbeing of its students and provides a range of services and resources to help students manage their mental health and wellbeing during their time at university.
That's great to hear! How do I go about booking an appointment with the Counseling Service?

If you're a current student at the University of Sheffield, you can book an appointment with the Counseling Service by completing a self-referral form on their website. 

Once you've completed the self-referral form, a member of the Counselling Service team will be in touch to arrange an initial consultation. During the consultation, you'll have the opportunity to discuss your concerns and work out a plan for ongoing support, if required.

The initial consultation is free-of-charge, and subsequent appointments with the Counselling Service are also free-of-charge.

If you need to speak to someone urgently outside of the Counseling Service's normal opening hours, you can contact the University's Nightline service. Nightline is a confidential listening service run by students for students, and is available every night during term-time between 8pm and 8am.
Is there any wait time to get an appointment, or are they usually available pretty quickly?

The wait time to get an appointment with the Counseling Service at the University of Sheffield usually varies depending on the demand for the service at a particular time. However, the Counseling Service strives to offer an initial consultation to all students within two weeks of receiving a completed self-referral form. This initial consultation will help you to identify your needs and determine the appropriate level of support required. If further sessions are needed, a regular appointment will be arranged on a day and time that is convenient for you and your therapist. In case of an emergency or a situation where you need immediate help, the Counseling Service also offers same-day appointments for urgent situations that cannot wait.
That's good to know. I'll fill out the self-referral form right away.
I'm glad I could help. Don't hesitate to reach out if you have any more questions or concerns. Take care!
It's a relief to know that there are resources available at the University of Sheffield to help with mental health concerns.

It's great to see that you want to take care of your mental health and well-being. The University of Sheffield is committed to supporting its students, and the Counseling Service is here to help whenever you need it. Don't hesitate to reach out if you need any more support. Take care!
